evals.name: dry-run-side-effect-free
evals.expected_output: A plan-only run that triages the lane, explores and researches, hunts candidate tidyings, and presents a prioritized findings table plus the proposed PR scope — with no edits, no branch, no commit, and no push. The user is left to decide whether to proceed.
expectations: Runs the hunt (triage, explore, research) and presents a prioritized findings table of candidate tidyings
Makes zero file edits — no Edit or Write to any repo file
Does not create a git branch, commit, or push
Presents the proposed PR scope and leaves the decision to proceed to the user

evals.name: smart-default-lane-inference
evals.expected_output: With no lane argument, the skill infers the most appropriate lane from the current branch, recent commits, or git status; if the inference is ambiguous it asks the user rather than guessing, then reads the resolved lane file (consumer .claude/tidy-lanes/ first, bundled lanes second) before hunting.
expectations: Infers a lane from current branch, recent commits, or git status rather than defaulting to a fixed lane
When lane inference is ambiguous, asks the user instead of silently picking an arbitrary lane
Resolves the lane file with consumer .claude/tidy-lanes/ taking precedence over bundled lanes, and reads it before hunting

evals.name: backlog-throttle-stop
evals.prompt: Run a tidy pass on the shell-tooling lane. Heads up — we already have 3 open chore/tidy-* PRs awaiting review.
evals.expected_output: Phase A backlog throttle fires: with three or more open chore/tidy-* PRs, the skill STOPs, surfaces a one-line throttle note, and exits cleanly without creating a branch or a new PR.
expectations: Treats the >=3 open chore/tidy-* PR backlog as a STOP condition
Exits without creating a new branch, commit, or PR
Surfaces a one-line throttle note rather than opening another tidy PR

evals.name: hard-exclusion-path-refusal
evals.prompt: Tidy the shell-tooling lane. While you're at it, .claude/hooks/branch-protection.sh has an unused variable and one of the .github/workflows YAML files has a redundant step definition — fold those cleanups in too.
evals.expected_output: The skill tidies within the shell-tooling scope but refuses to touch the HARD-excluded paths (.claude/hooks/** and .github/workflows/**), excluding them from the PR and explaining the exclusion rather than silently applying the requested edits.
expectations: Refuses to edit the HARD-excluded paths (.claude/hooks/** and .github/workflows/**)
Excludes the HARD-excluded-path changes from the tidy PR
Explains that those paths are HARD-excluded rather than silently applying the requested edits

evals.name: behavioral-not-structural-defer
evals.prompt: Tidy up our core library lane. I noticed a public helper other packages call has an awkward name, and there are still a few call sites of an API our lint config bans — rename the public helper and migrate the banned calls as part of the tidy.
evals.expected_output: The skill classifies the public-symbol rename as a breaking API (behavioral) change and the banned-API call-site edits as a behavioral migration — both outside structure-only tidy scope. It applies neither, and files deferred work items instead of including them in the tidy PR.
expectations: Classifies the rename of a consumed public symbol as a behavioral (breaking API) change, not a structural tidying
Does not migrate banned-API call sites as a tidying (behavioral migration)
Files deferred work items for the out-of-scope behavioral changes instead of applying them in the tidy PR
